default.name: run_in_wasm_interpreter
default.description: Run python or javascript code in an isolated WebAssembly sandbox and get back its stdout, stderr, and error. Beyond computation, parsing, and data work, code can call external HTTP APIs, keep data across runs, and serve HTTP requests. Outbound HTTP is denied unless the application permits the destination. JavaScript uses the standard `fetch`. If the destination is not allowed, fetch rejects; the runtime may report the generic error "An error occurred while using the host API". Python uses `from spin_sdk.http import send, Request` and `send(Request(method, url, headers, body))`; urllib, http.client, and requests are not available. If the destination is not allowed, the guard returns HttpRequestDenied, surfaced as `Err(ErrorCode_HttpRequestDenied())`. Network permissions are configured by the application and cannot be changed through tool arguments. Persistent storage is available only when enabled by the application, which also controls the storage namespace. Runs in the same namespace share stored KV data, whether they use the same language or different languages. Sharing depends on the namespace, not on reusing an Interpreter client object; different namespaces are isolated. JavaScript: `import { openDefault } from "@spinframework/spin-kv"`, then get/set or getJson/setJson. Python: `from spin_sdk import key_value`, then `key_value.open_default()` with get/set (values are bytes). HTTP handlers: supply input to run a handler against that request and get its HTTP response. JavaScript exports `default { async fetch(request) {} }`, awaiting all async work before it returns the Response; Python defines `handle_request(request)` and may return an iterable of str or bytes chunks to stream the body. Python includes numpy, pydantic, pyyaml, regex, beautifulsoup4, jinja2, markdown, tabulate, sqlalchemy, tiktoken (no built-in encodings: get_encoding() fails, so pass your own mergeable_ranks to tiktoken.Encoding), and the standard library except its networking modules. JavaScript (TypeScript syntax is accepted) includes lodash, zod, date-fns, dayjs, cheerio, node-html-parser, js-yaml, uuid, ulidx, and nanoid. For other npm packages, list them in dependencies as name -> semver ranges; they are bundled before the run. Use ESM import, never require(). Each run is a fresh instance: variables and globals do not carry over. When storage is enabled, persist state in the key-value store. There is no filesystem, shell, subprocess, or raw socket, and no runtime pip install. stdout and stderr are each capped at 256 KB.

code.description: The complete program to run. Print results to stdout. JavaScript supports top-level await: await all asynchronous work directly. Never leave floating promises (an un-awaited async IIFE, main() call, or timer); work still running when the program ends is discarded without any output or error.

dependencies.description: JavaScript only. Extra npm dependencies as name -> semver ranges. Use ESM import; Python cannot add packages.

input.description: Mock HTTP request for handler code. Supplying it runs a JavaScript `export default { fetch(request) {} }` or Python `handle_request(request)` handler and returns its HTTP response.

body.description: Request body as a string or JSON value.
